body.p: Claims 1, 9, 12 and 13 stand rejected on the ground of non-statutory obviousness-type
body.h1: double patenting as allegedly being unpatentable over claims 1-2, 9-10 and 12-13 of U.S. Patent
body.p: No. 11,911,910. Claims 1, 8, 12 and 13 stand rejected on the ground of non-statutory obviousness-type double patenting as allegedly being unpatentable over claims 1-2, 8, 12 and 13 of U.S. Patent No. 11,529,734.
Claims 1, 8, 12 and 13 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Anderson et al (US Patent Publication No. 2019/0321115 Al, hereinafter "Anderson").
Claim 1 is now amended to incorporate subject matter of allowable dependent claim 2.

Dependent claim 10 is now re-written in independent form but without the limitations of its intermediate claim 9. Nevertheless, it is submitted that claim 10 as amended here does overcome both the double patenting and the obviousness rejections.
Accordingly, all claims now pending upon entry of this amendment, namely claims 1 and 3-20 are submitted to be in condition for allowance.

It should be noted that not all the assertions made in the Office Action, particularly those with respect to un-argued limitations in the independent claims and in other dependent claims, might have been addressed here, in the interest of conciseness. In other words, Applicant has not acquiesced to the positions taken in those rejections and reserves the right to challenge any of the assertions made in the Office Action by the Examiner, with respect to for example any relied upon art references and how they would relate to Applicants' claim language and particularly certain limitations in the independent claims that have not been argued above. Applicant reserves the right to re-visit the positions taken in those rejections, should they arise in the future, for example when an appeal is filed or when Applicant files a continuing application. Applicant also reserves the right to swear behind or otherwise remove an improper art reference.

The Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge any deficiency in fees which may be required when considering any submission regarding this application under 37 C.F.R. §§ 1.16- 1.17, or credit any overpayment, to Deposit Account No. 606306.
In the event a telephone conversation expedites the prosecution of this application, the Examiner may reach the undersigned at (818) 826-3757.
